basis: Complete assigned brief and released plan; frozen investigator package; both complementary critique packages; direct primary-source rechecks listed below.

sources.title: ReaderBuilder in csv - Rust
sources.version_or_commit: csv 1.4.0 displayed on docs.rs page; latest URL is rolling; no source commit shown.
sources.locator: ReaderBuilder; has_headers and flexible methods.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: First record is treated as header by default; unequal record field counts error by default; flexible(true) disables that arity check.
sources.applicability: Explicit parser profile and no unreviewed header/arity assumptions; parser choice remains open.

sources.title: Reader in csv 1.4.0 - Rust
sources.version_or_commit: csv crate 1.4.0.
sources.locator: read_record/read_byte_record at lines 597-633; configuration/error notes at lines 95-103.
sources.observed_operation: Opened version-pinned API docs and inspected incremental record and encoding notes.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Reusable record reads return Result and provide positions; StringRecord strictly requires UTF-8; byte APIs allow retaining undecoded bytes.
sources.applicability: Streaming, bounded record allocation, accurate error location and explicit encoding handling.

sources.title: Rust csv tutorial
sources.version_or_commit: csv 1.4.0 companion docs; rolling URL; no commit shown.
sources.locator: Unequal-length record example and header-detection note (page lines 146-153 and 342).
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: The shown parser reports an unequal-length record; it explicitly does not heuristically decide whether the first row is a header.
sources.applicability: Tests must pin header behavior and confirm late structural errors reach the caller.

sources.title: RFC 4180: Common Format and MIME Type for Comma-Separated Values (CSV) Files
sources.version_or_commit: RFC 4180, October 2005, Informational.
sources.locator: Sections 2-3, including field-count, quoting and interoperability notes.
sources.observed_operation: Opened RFC Editor record and text.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Comma-separated profile; equal field counts are recommended; quotes permit embedded commas/line breaks; RFC notes implementations differ and it is not a complete universal CSV specification.
sources.applicability: Useful parser baseline, not authority for every logger's dialect, nulls, types or units.

sources.title: W3C Metadata Vocabulary for Tabular Data
sources.version_or_commit: W3C Recommendation, 17 December 2015.
sources.locator: Column properties datatype/null/required and dialect vocabulary; security considerations.
sources.observed_operation: Opened W3C recommendation and inspected metadata vocabulary.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Column null markers are configurable; absent a null property, empty string is the default marker; metadata may rename/ignore columns, and transformation definitions can execute code.
sources.applicability: Profile structure inspiration only; logger semantics must be confirmed and imported metadata/code must be treated as untrusted.

sources.title: DuckDB CSV Auto Detection
sources.version_or_commit: Rolling current documentation; exact engine/docs build version is not displayed.
sources.locator: Sample Size and Detection Steps.
sources.observed_operation: Opened DuckDB Foundation docs and inspected sample/default/inference options.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Type inference samples 20,480 rows by default; sample_size=-1 scans all rows for sampling; dialect candidates include comma, pipe, semicolon, tab; all_varchar disables type inference.
sources.applicability: Compare as alternate parser; sample-based inference is provisional and should not govern stored meaning.

sources.title: DuckDB Reading Faulty CSV Files
sources.version_or_commit: Rolling current documentation; exact engine/docs build version is not displayed.
sources.locator: Structural Errors and Anatomy of a CSV Error.
sources.observed_operation: Opened DuckDB Foundation parser error-handling docs.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Structural errors stop scanning and error by default; docs also support skip and reject-table options; default maximum line size is 2,097,152 bytes.
sources.applicability: A tolerant skip mode cannot be the silent commit path; line-size and reject handling must be explicit.

sources.title: DuckDB issue 13660: Conversion Error of a DATE column when reading a file to insert in table
sources.version_or_commit: Upstream DuckDB issue; report/conversation includes 2024 date; executable version not established in inspected excerpt.
sources.locator: Issue reproduction and suggested explicit type/sample_size adjustments.
sources.observed_operation: Opened upstream issue and read reproduction and maintainer/user discussion.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Reported date conversion problem with auto-detected type/date format; suggested setting a type or scanning more rows; format list limitations also discussed.
sources.applicability: Keep mixed date strings visible, pin parsing rules and include late-format samples; an issue report is not proof of current behavior.

sources.title: DuckDB issue 12338: read_csv behavior across versions
sources.version_or_commit: Issue reports v0.10.1 working versus v0.10.3 and v1.0.0 failures in one StringIO/encoding/CSV path; later closed by PR 13597; first fixed release not established here.
sources.locator: Issue reproduction and version comparison; see linked closing PR 13597.
sources.observed_operation: Opened upstream issue and inspected versioned report.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: A specific API/input encoding/newline path changed across releases; issue was later closed, but the inspected issue does not name a released first-fixed version.
sources.applicability: Pin exact parser build and preserve versioned regression fixtures; do not generalize a historical report to current builds.

sources.title: DuckDB Transaction Management
sources.version_or_commit: Rolling current documentation; exact engine/docs build version is not displayed.
sources.locator: Starting, committing, rolling back and multi-statement transaction sections.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Explicit begin/commit/rollback supported; a failing statement in an implicit multi-statement transaction rolls preceding statements back; transaction claims are ACID/snapshot-isolated in docs.
sources.applicability: Candidate local transaction engine; test the exact embedded release and database workload.

sources.title: DuckDB Concurrency
sources.version_or_commit: Rolling current documentation; exact engine/docs build version is not displayed.
sources.locator: Optimistic Concurrency Control and Troubleshooting.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Concurrent writes to same rows can conflict and must be retried; file-lock warning for shared/network directories.
sources.applicability: Relevant to concurrent preview/apply and local-file placement; retry must not change user decisions.

sources.title: SQLite Transaction
sources.version_or_commit: SQLite language documentation; rolling page, no version-specific snapshot shown.
sources.locator: Read transactions versus write transactions.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Multiple readers can coexist; only one simultaneous write transaction; a read-to-write upgrade can fail SQLITE_BUSY.
sources.applicability: Database work belongs after parsing/preview; define busy, retry and concurrent preview invalidation behavior.

sources.title: SQLite Savepoints
sources.version_or_commit: SQLite language documentation; rolling page, no version-specific snapshot shown.
sources.locator: Savepoint release and nesting semantics.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Releasing an inner savepoint merges into its parent and does not write/commit independently; outer rollback still undoes it.
sources.applicability: Keep one outer transaction for whole-file atomicity; chunk savepoints do not make partial commits safe.

sources.title: SQLite ON CONFLICT Clause
sources.version_or_commit: SQLite language documentation; UPSERT separately available since 3.24.0 (2018-06-04).
sources.locator: ROLLBACK, ABORT, FAIL, IGNORE and REPLACE algorithms.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: ABORT is default; FAIL preserves earlier changes in a failing statement; IGNORE skips conflicting rows; REPLACE deletes prior conflicting rows before insert.
sources.applicability: Do not silently skip or delete prior observations; wrap accepted apply in an outer rollback-capable transaction.

sources.title: SQLite Write-Ahead Logging and WAL-reset bug history
sources.version_or_commit: Official page states defect likely in SQLite 3.7.0 through 3.51.2; fixed in 3.51.3 (2026-03-13) and later, with backports.
sources.locator: Section 11, WAL-Reset Bug.
sources.observed_operation: Opened SQLite official WAL page and read failure history.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Corruption race requires WAL mode, at least two connections to the same DB and concurrent write/checkpoint timing; rare but serious.
sources.applicability: If WAL is chosen, pin a fixed release and test the supported concurrency pattern.

sources.title: Chrono LocalResult
sources.version_or_commit: Chrono 0.4.45 displayed on docs.rs page; latest URL is rolling.
sources.locator: Single, Ambiguous and None variants.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Ambiguous means a fold with earliest/latest possibilities; None means a gap or resolution error.
sources.applicability: Show explicit zone ambiguity/gap and require a user/source rule before creating an instant.

sources.title: UCUM Specification
sources.locator: Version header; unit symbols and canonical form notes; Example Unit Terms.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Machine code system for units; symbols can be case-sensitive; some canonical conversions require functions; not every possible term is exhaustively enumerated.
sources.applicability: Use as a validation/conversion vocabulary only after the measured quantity and logger symbol are confirmed.

sources.title: OGC SensorThings API Part 1: Sensing Version 1.1
sources.version_or_commit: OGC 18-088, SensorThings API Part 1: Sensing, Version 1.1.
sources.locator: Chapter 7.3, PDF pages 26-27; observation/event-time/model discussion.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Observation context includes event time, FeatureOfInterest, ObservedProperty and procedure/sensor; standard permits proprietary sensor interfaces.
sources.applicability: Candidate vocabulary for semantic identity fields; not proof that logger files expose these fields or use standard IDs.

sources.title: RFC 3339: Date and Time on the Internet: Timestamps
sources.version_or_commit: RFC 3339, July 2002, Standards Track.
sources.locator: Sections 4.2-4.4 and 5.6.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Defined full Internet date-times carry Z or numeric offset; unqualified local time is not an unambiguous instant; -00:00 specifically records unknown local offset.
sources.applicability: Preserve ambiguous local wall times and obtain an explicit source timezone rather than defaulting to OS local time.

sources.title: Rust csv maintainer response: malformed whitespace/quote case
sources.version_or_commit: Maintainer discussion dated 2023-06-29; crate release/commit not given.
sources.locator: Accepted answer, lines 194-197.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Maintainer says the example input is invalid and csv attempts to salvage it; recommends fixing source data or bespoke handling.
sources.applicability: Late malformed syntax must be validated against intended grammar; successful parser output can still be wrong.

sources.title: Atomic Commit In SQLite
sources.version_or_commit: Official SQLite documentation; rolling page, no release-specific snapshot shown. This article explicitly describes rollback-journal mode; WAL uses a different commit mechanism.
sources.locator: Introduction and Hardware Assumptions, rendered lines 117-146; rollback-mode applicability, filesystem and fsync assumptions, and sync caveats.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official SQLite atomic-commit page and reviewed its stated mode scope, hardware assumptions, and flush/fsync caveats.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: The page describes apparent atomic commit for a single transaction in rollback mode, under stated operating-system/storage assumptions. It says WAL uses a different mechanism and notes broken flush/fsync can undermine power-loss guarantees.
sources.applicability: Supports narrowing crash/durability claims and testing the pinned journal mode, filesystem and supported platform combination.

reviser_primary_rechecks.title: DuckDB CSV Auto Detection
reviser_primary_rechecks.documentation_edition_displayed: DuckDB 1.5 current; URL remains rolling and this is not a selected engine build
reviser_primary_rechecks.locator: Sample Size and Detection Steps; official page lines 515-529 and 563-620
reviser_primary_rechecks.observed_operation: Reopened official DuckDB documentation and checked current sample behavior and detection/validation distinction.
reviser_primary_rechecks.governing_condition_default_exception: Type inference defaults to 20,480 rows; sample_size=-1 reads the full file for sampling. Seekable regular files may be sampled from different locations; non-seekable compressed/stdin inputs are sampled from the beginning.
reviser_primary_rechecks.applicability: Detection and full-file sampling are not EOF validation under the confirmed profile.

reviser_primary_rechecks.title: SQLite Transaction
reviser_primary_rechecks.version_or_commit: Official rolling language page; updated 2026-02-18; no engine build specified
reviser_primary_rechecks.locator: Read/write concurrency, implicit vs explicit transactions, COMMIT and SQLITE_BUSY; especially section 2.3 and response to errors
reviser_primary_rechecks.observed_operation: Reopened official transaction documentation and checked busy commit and transaction-state behavior.
reviser_primary_rechecks.governing_condition_default_exception: Only one simultaneous write transaction. SQLITE_BUSY from COMMIT can leave the transaction active and retryable; certain I/O/full/interrupt errors may or may not roll back the full transaction.
reviser_primary_rechecks.applicability: Define bounded commit retry or explicit rollback and confirm terminal transaction state; compare preview generation before writes.

reviser_primary_rechecks.title: SQLite ON CONFLICT Clause
reviser_primary_rechecks.version_or_commit: Official page updated 2025-11-22; no engine build specified
reviser_primary_rechecks.locator: ABORT, FAIL, IGNORE and REPLACE algorithms
reviser_primary_rechecks.observed_operation: Reopened official conflict documentation and checked statement vs transaction effects.
reviser_primary_rechecks.governing_condition_default_exception: ABORT is default and backs out only the failed statement, preserving earlier statements in the active transaction; FAIL may retain earlier row changes in the failed statement; IGNORE skips rows; REPLACE deletes conflicting rows.
reviser_primary_rechecks.applicability: Application must explicitly roll back outer transaction after apply error/cancel.

reviser_primary_rechecks.title: SQLite Write-Ahead Logging and WAL-reset bug history
reviser_primary_rechecks.version_or_commit: Official page updated 2026-08-25; fix in 3.51.3+, with listed backports 3.44.6 and 3.50.7
reviser_primary_rechecks.locator: Overview (single-file/multi-ATTACH atomicity); Section 11, WAL-reset bug and conditions
reviser_primary_rechecks.observed_operation: Reopened official WAL page and checked mode, cross-database atomicity, affected/fixed releases and race conditions.
reviser_primary_rechecks.governing_condition_default_exception: WAL defect through 3.51.2 requires WAL, two or more connections to one file, and coincident write/checkpoint activity. WAL transactions across ATTACHed files are not atomic as a set.
reviser_primary_rechecks.applicability: Conditional WAL build floor and test; keep promised atomic records/provenance in one database file. Does not establish rollback-mode risk.

reviser_primary_rechecks.title: Atomic Commit In SQLite
reviser_primary_rechecks.version_or_commit: Official rolling documentation; no release-specific snapshot; article explicitly covers rollback-journal mode
reviser_primary_rechecks.locator: Introduction and Hardware Assumptions, sections 1–2; distinguish WAL mechanism
reviser_primary_rechecks.observed_operation: Reopened official atomic-commit article and checked mode scope and storage assumptions.
reviser_primary_rechecks.governing_condition_default_exception: Description applies only to rollback-journal mode; WAL uses a different mechanism. Commit durability depends on stated storage, OS, filesystem and flush assumptions.
reviser_primary_rechecks.applicability: Name and test the actual shipped journal mode, synchronous configuration, filesystem and platform before making crash/power-loss promises.
